text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Pro Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Pro

text_fidelity_a:
TenmaTec Voice Recorder with Playback,80GB Voice Activated Recorder with DSP Noise Reduction,Dual Microphones, Mp3,Speaker,Password Protect,for Music,Overdubbing,Studio,Dictation,Interview The build quality of this little portable recorder is great. It's metal, not plastic, and has a nice heft and feels durable. It looks great. And audio quality is very good. It comes with a micro SD card already installed and ready to go. It also comes with a set of ear buds, a lavalier microphone which can be used instead of the built-in mics, a cord for line-in recording, and a USB charging cord. No charger is included. And it does not come with a protective pouch or sleeve. But it is boxed nicely.

It records in user-selectable WAV or MP3 formats in various selectable bitrates. It has adjustable gain control and a noise reduction function. One important function for voice recording is the ability to monitor while recording using ear buds or headphones, and this recorder has that capability. The display screen isn't as sharp and clear as it is portrayed in the listing photos, but it is decent.

Now for the minor negatives, for which I dinged a star off the review rating. One is the printing labeling the buttons on the one I received is only a little lighter than the color of the recorder, making them very hard to read. That means you have to memorize the button location and functions or keep the user manual handy for reference. And that leads to the second negative, and that is the print in the user manual is tiny. Really tiny. I looked for a PDF version online and couldn't find one. The manual suggests visiting the brand's web site, but neither the manual nor the box provide a URL. Or even the listing brand name (Tenmatec) for that matter. I wound taking photographs of the manual pages with a tablet so I could enlarge them for easier reading. The other minor negative is that it has no USB-C port, only a micro USB for recharging or connecting to a computer for moving files around.

Other than that it's a good recorder. It has one-button functionality (although there is a slight delay when starting a recording while it starts up). Because of its metal construction and heft it feels good in-hand and looks really good.
text_fidelity_b: TenmaTec Voice Recorder with Playback,80GB Voice Activated Recorder with DSP Noise Reduction,Dual Microphones, Mp3,Speaker,Password Protect,for Music,Overdubbing,Studio,Dictation,Interview

PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B) If you're an iphone user, you're probably wondering whether to buy these Pioneer wireless headphones or the Apple version. The Pioneer price is about 1/3 cheaper than Apple. The Pioneer earbuds fit in your ear, so you get much better sound and much better sound isolation. These are nowhere near as detailed or loud as similarly priced wired headphones, but that's true of all wireless Bluetooth earbuds. I will say the connection is stable and not noisy, so these are better than most cheap Bluetooth earbuds. There is some bass, but don't work well for bass-heavy music. Maximum volume is just OK. Battery life is only about 3 hours per charge (compared to 5 hours for Apple), then you have to put the earbuds back in the case for a 1 hour charge. 3 hours may be enough for you; you have to decide, but 5 hours is certainly going to be more interesting to most people. The charging case is much larger than the Apple charging case. The case is 3.3 inches long and 2.2 inches wide. These case is to big to fit comfortably in my pants pocket, so I would only carry it with me in a backpack or purse.

Usage is pretty simple. They paired easily with my phone as a normal Bluetooth device. The buttons on the headphones are easy to use. They are comfortable in my ears. They are secure enough so far, never feeling like they are going to fall out. They are not noticeably heavy like some earbuds can be. When in my ears, they are much less ugly than the Apple earbuds.

I would give these 5 stars for the price and performance if the sound and battery life were better. Frankly, I've tried a few different totally wireless earbuds and been less than impressed by all of them. Bluetooth headphones that have a wire connecting the two pieces can be had for much lower prices and have much better sound quality and much better battery life. Removing the wire just doesn't seem worth the downsides to me.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B)

That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Sony Cyber-shot DSC -H 55.
I have owned two other cameras in the past. My last Camera, before this one, was a 12 Megapixel. And I thought it, at first to be ALL THAT. This was only because my previous camera had been a four Megapixel. I was so impressed with the increase in the resolution that is all I could see was the ability to crop photos to a better end then I had been able to. After the newness had worn off I began to realize the Cameron was just a lemon. So with this camera, that mistake will not happen again. The (14 Megapixel) of this Sony camera is not that different from my (12 Megapixel) camera that I am replacing. So I will look past the resolution difference with ease.
However the (10 x) zoom lens is NEW. Not only to me, but to all (point and shoot) cameras I have ever seen. Now, the 10 x zoom lens that I am talking about is NOT digital zoom. But rather, purely optical. There is a digital zoom offered in the menus of this camera. But I simply turned this feature off. If I want to do any digital zoom, I'll do it in Photoshop on my own time.
Other perks include; a battery and charger. The battery is lithium. And knowing that a lithium battery must be conditioned before its true capacity can ever be obtained. And even before the battery had been `conditioned' it was still able to take approximately 400 shots. And of course four or five HRS of me playing around in the menus with the features. And I know from past experience this can be one of the biggest power drains on a camera battery. And this is only the first cycle. I don't foresee a need in my future to buy a spear battery.
While I am on the subject of batteries, I need to mention. The battery charger is a cute little thing. The part of the plug that actually goes into the wall will fold into the plastic housing. So it is not a burdensome piece of machinery to store. And the whole thing is extremely small. It is only 3"x2"x1". To me that sounds ridiculously small, and if it were not right here in front of me I might not even believe. But it is true. It will fit in my small camera case, instead of the drawer. I already have enough mess around my room.
Also about batteries, there is a handy little gauge, on the LCD screen, that reports the amount of battery left by a four bar indicator (like a cell phone).
I spoke earlier about the massive zoom lens. But I didn't even tell how this camera can also take a macro picture up to about 8" away at full wide angle (zoom out). The 8" I just spoke could be off a little by + or - an inch. The manual that could tell me for sure is over there in that box, and I am over here. And I'm a lazy person.
I'm really impressed at how small this camera is. It will fit very nicely, with lots of room to spare, in my chest pocket. I do wear a 2X shirt, but there is so much room left over, I bet you could fit this camera in a large size pocket. I haven't had a chance to test it; I'm just using my best estimate. On outings, being able to tuck this camera away in my pocket will be way awesome. And it is so light weight.
And it weighs very, very little for such a nice camera. I have a cordless optical mouse hooked up to this computer. So by comparing weight, the mouse is the more heavy of the two.
I think I have touched on the biggest topics I can think of at this sitting, but to sum this up. This is the best camera I (personally) have ever owned. This would include 2 other digital cameras (one SLR type & one point and shoot) and a couple `film cameras' 110 and a 35mm SLR my uncle left to me. And after comparing it with all the other ones available at the stores, it IS the best. I compare every time a store has a display, to see if mine is still better. Even some of the `better' SLR types that sell for $100's, fall short. I would be really upset to see that a little `point & shoot' can beat my $800 `SLR type' camera.
At $225 and $25 3 year extended warranty from Samsclub, I have a new gizmo and I did not break the bank.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

text_fidelity_a: CozyPhones Sleep Headphones - Over Ear Headphones from Ultra Thin Cool Mesh Wired for Side Sleepers, Meditation, Running, Laptop, and Phone - Purple Lycra I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA) For the price, this is a decent set of gaming headphones. The build quality is perfectly fine for the price point. It doesn't feel as rock solid as more expensive brands, but feels like it will certainly stand up to normal usage.

The comfort is borderline. It feels fine for up to about an hour of usage, then the ear cups start to become somewhat uncomfortable and the headband pinches a bit. It's not the best set for hours and hours of usage, but for "normal" wear times I didn't have any problems.

The sound quality is quite good. Nice amount of bass response without sounding muddy. I also found it to have more than good enough sound quality for watching movies, with the dialogue coming through clearly. It's not the best for listening to music (the mid and upper ranges are a bit constrained) but for it's intended purpose of a gaming set, no complaints at all regarding sound quality.

My major problem was with range. I love the fact that these are wireless, but placement is critical. I'd lose the signal if I didn't vary much from a specific spot near the wireless adapter. Moving just a bit out of the "zone" killed the connection. That was a disappointment since, while I didn't expect to be able to roam around the house with them on, I did expect to be able to leave my chair and go a short distance without breaking the connection. No problems with signal strength when seated or within a few feet of the adapter, but hit and miss when moving more than a few feet away.

Other than the range issue, this is a pretty good value in a gaming headphone set.
text_fidelity_b: Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White) This tablet has entirely streamlined my educational, professional, and personal productivity. I will preface this by saying I chose this tablet (as my very first tablet of any kind) after 5 WEEKS of research and hours and hours of reading the manual, watching video of reviews, unboxing, customization, how-to's, tips and tricks, and specific software guides. I had the nexus 10 in my amazon shopping cart when I first came across this tablet. I will nowhere in this review compare this to an apple device- I have never and will never own one- personal preference, I wholeheartedly believe iOS is sufficient or ideal for a lot of people's use, just not ever going to be for mine. As background, I am in an international DVM program whose laptop just crashed and all 600+gigs of my life were backed up but now only floating in cyberspace so my requirements were a little heady for a tablet-

a) deal with extensive editing and review of PDFs, PPTs, DOCs, XLXS, etc 14-17hrs a day (terms range from 21-24 credits, 4-5hrs of lecture straight, 3-4 hrs of lab with no access to outlet in many labs). Also when I say edit I don't just mean take notes on I also mean incorporate text, figures, etc from textbooks, websites, and other documents.

b) Be a textbook reader and rarely a e-book reader (novels for fun!) Need to access my extensive kindle library, plus some google books and a few Elsevier/pageburst textbooks. Also this needs to be something I am comfortable and accepting of to literally study off of, enough to give up my previous preferring to only study off of paper/actual printed out notes

c) Allow for flawless email, web chat, skype video and text, some web browsing, and file transfer... all on an absolutely horrible school wireless and LAN setup, unpredictable power availability, etc.

d) Streaming and downloading of podcasts, video, MRI, CT, radiographs, and ECG's

e) Be portable to the clinic and the farms for patient-side transcription, recording, etc

f) Get me through the 5-6hr flight and all the airport time!

g) Occasionally watch videos/listen to things for fun

h) Most importantly, due to a dominant hand injury, multiple surgeries, and continued required hand therapy/rehab, I am currently able to write again but not to type with that hand. I therefore wanted a tablet that was stylus intensive- not just for notes, but for navigation, etc. THIS is what made me give up that wonderful squeaky clean android OS of the nexus 10! (I still thing that is probably the best thing for people that want an android tablet but don't NEED a stylus)
So my tablet arrived flawless and flawlessly. The display is beautiful, if anything the screen is too bright- I'm aware my eyes are light sensitive so this won't match with the majority of people but if I do turn my brightness on at all I don't believe I've ever gone above 15%, though I'm sure there will be some case videos poorly and darkly shot that I may need to in the future.

i) at least temporarily, replace my laptop and download and have as much of my backed up laptop files as possible

The tablet was quickly populated with the apps from my HTC phone and google account. The account set up for everything was quick and easy. The initial 2 updates were completed with no adverse signs. Navigation was great, no lag, and I quickly cleared out the stock widgets, set up my panes, and then went into settings.... I activated Developer options and did some customization and disabling there, but most of the disabling I did in app manager, device, and controls. There are very helpful guides out there if you're not sure which apps are safe to disable as well as a "Guide: Longer Battery Life- How You're Being Robbed on XDA that takes you step by step in maximizing your tablet. It was not created at the time when I cleaned up mine but it would've helped greatly!

Here is the gist. The tablet comes crammed full of software and capabilities that I don't need or want. The My Magazine app, a lot of the touchwiz stuff, the eye movement sensors(smart screen), the hand gesture stuff, reading mode, voice control, motions/palm motions, all of that is just a constant battery drain and I will never use them. They were disabled and the vibration feedback for everything was also turned off.

Battery Report: This tablet was shipped within the US twice, and was brought internationally on a plan 4 days later. It was accidently left on the ENTIRE time for about 8 days with six apps up on standby. It arrived with 18% battery left. I use it for 15-17hours a day and end up having to charge it 2-3hrs per about ever 24hr period to get it back to 100. I can use it while it is charging and it will still positively charge during use.

USE FOR A STUDENT: It has replaced textbooks, laptop, printer, scanner, and painstakenly editing and customizing notes and making documents for me. Disclaimer: as someone who used to be able to type 130+ words per minute, I'll make perfectly clear, if you prefer to type and plan on typing a LOT tablet touchscreen keyboards SUCK. This is a fact of life. You can get used to them, you can get proficient at them, but you'll still probably hate it and you're going to need a physical keyboard case/add on if you do a lot of typing of documents or emails. Now, this tablet is made for a stylus. This is not just a peculiarly edged simple piece of plastic that you can buy for just about any touchscreen device and kind of use as a writing device. This is the s-pen, a WACOM and this device and stylus is designed to maximize the experience so you are writing or drawing digitally with an experience just like on paper. Examples- the harder you press the more solid and thicker your pencil/pen/brush/highlighter/calligraphy/etc line. The button on the stylus brings up air command which can be super helpful and it also allows quick screen shots. The stylus allows for fine website navigation that allows you to open drop down windows etc as mouse would. It also offers things a real pen/pencil cant- selective erasing, and selection for drag/drop/copy/paste of ANYTHING to ANYWHERE. You're typing notes and see a great figure and text on a website, you can freehand or rectangular circle what you want and put it into your document. Then you can resize/edit. It's great. I've been using the Snote app for everything thus far, I have made short futile attempts with Lecture Notes and Evernote but I couldn't really get anywhere. I'm not going to give up on then, I just need to research them more to see if I can eventually get them to do what I want and then I can compare them to Snote.

USE FOR A PROFESSIONAL: So far, this has been wonderful. I can seamlessly take notes, look up references, voice record my exam findings, and awkwardly as only a tablet is, take video and pictures of patient's during an exam for later review. (Extremely helpful during lameness and neuro exams for the file). Collaborative documents through Polaris office and google drive is exceptional- as fast as a laptop and more portable, and better screen size than a smartphone. It runs better than the school computers for running presentations off of onto projectors. I can also have students I tutor digitally sign- literally our weekly sheets and submit them via email with one step- completely negating the awesome printer and scanner I brought down here.

USE FOR A CONSUMER: I find this tablet beautiful for watching movies and videos and the sound is great. In a classroom of 50 people chatting between classes I have no problem hearing the speakers among the hub but there are completely valid reports that even cranked the sound might get lost a little if you're in a very loud close crowd. Sound improves with earbuds but the initial audio set up app (basically a hearing test and then a customized audio scheme for you) was startling when it compared the stock/base line settings to what it came up with for ME.

USE FOR AN ARTIST: I'm still learning and adapting, I'll never turn to this instead of actual physical art supplies and paper but it is fun and I can really see myself doing more digital than before. It has been especially nice for graphic design, photoshopping, etc.

USE AS A LEFTY: no issues except see below for one thing that affects both right and left handers...

ISSUES: 1) One day after about a week of ownership, my battery was in the upper 80's, I was taking some notes and about 2hrs later I looked at the status bar and it was 29%. I went into Battery in Settings, and the s-pen interface was responsible for 80% of the battery use. I shut down and then restarted and it's never happened again. Similarly the Android OS did the same thing at a later instance but again it was a one time thing and in both cases the battery recharged speedily after and stayed charged.
2) Snote- I have had weird episodes where an import fails, or it force closes itself repeatedly when I try to rename or change the cover of one particular document. After this erratic behavior occurred twice in three days and completely clearing and restarting Snote from scratch (everything backed up and replaced on my Samsung account) to no avail, I did a factory reset. The last ¾ of my ownership have seen no such problems any more. I will warn you that if you wipe out S note and you start from scratch in it and re-transfer all your SNote files back in, if you have a lot of really big files, it can take a really long time to re-populate.
3) The menu/return and physical home button- occasionally based on the desk I'm at, if my arm isn't supported and my wrist is resting fully on the edge of the tablet, these buttons will get pressed while I'm writing. Its purely an annoyance and doesn't affect the writing or do anything but I definitely have to reposition if I find I'm getting lazy on holding my wrist up at these desks.

Wrap up: I only use in landscape, it's just like writing on a portrait piece of paper except you can also zoom. I got used to writing on the tablet and the tiny stylus very quickly but there are compatible Samsung styli of various widths and sizes out there as well. I thought about waiting for the new 12.2 whose screen is literally a full piece of paper landscape, but I realized this is perfect for me and more portable than the 12.2 will be (this thing can just squeeze into one of the pockets on one of my lab coats. I was planning on having to use the Nova launcher to avoid any lag but truly, this tablet was a speed demon already and I eventually got Nova solely for the customization ability and cleaner interface. It allows me to avoid more things I don't use and I didn't lose ANY of the software I do.

Bottom line, RESEARCH! PREPARE! And there will STILL BE A LEARNING CURVE! But it will be based on discovering unexpected cool features instead of on frustration). If you won't heavily use the stylus, don't spend the money on this tablet. If you're just curious if you could "get into a stylus" try one out first but prepare first so you can use it to the full advantage while you're there. Also, I came from NO tablet and no Samsung/Note experience and there are changes between the previous model and this. You don't actually lose much but things are moved around and different. Don't be scared to optimize it, I'm not talking rooting, though adventurous forays into that terrain have finally arrived as well. In conclusion I love it, it has made things so much more efficient for me, I get a lot DONE with it and it's basically all I have to carry around. I purchased the 32gig tablet plus a 64gig Sandisk XC which installed and worked like a charm. There are annoyances that come up but any issue I have had I have been able to fix. I have everything safely backed up on Carbonite and there's a million ways to sync all of your accounts if you chose (note some of this may be unnecessary or frequency can be dialed back too)

It performs and looks beautiful and I am still learning.

EDIT: FLASH PLAYER: This tablet absolutely supports flash. Youtube and embedded flash worked right out of the box, however, to watch my amazon video's etc, I just downloaded the following file- I cannot post the actual link but it's a drop box file. Install this and make sure flash is enabled in your browser settings/plugins and it will work in the stock browser, Dolphin, and Mozilla. Some people also recommend having your browser set to View Desktop site.

Edit 12/15/2014: Please see my comment under product question- "Can you use amazon prime video on the galaxy 10.1 2014 ed? asked by Judith C. Love on November 14, 2013" for instructions and the direct link for flash file

Edit 02/2017: My tablet got slammed by careless sleep-deprived brain addled 4th year vet students and the screen got shattered in the upper right corner. Still useable, not any real issues but concern about the little chips and cracks gradually loosening and only being held together by the screen protector I was itching to replace due to scratches but now couldnt, left me with the desire to replace as I was 4 months out of my extended warranty. Call it coincidence but literally as I powered up the replacement, this original tablet FAILED. The screen doesn't illuminate. At certain angle/light you can see it's on but there is no way for me to see well enough to unlock the screen and at least access over 3 years of my life on the original tablet. I am 99% convinced this is secondary to the trauma/screen break, and I had nearly everything backed up via Carbonite on the original except for the past few months of random downloads. Still, I am grieved and wanted a moment of silence.

Yes we had great times together but I am truly sad and a bit devastated because the replacement came with OS updates that I had been actively refusing to install for the past year. Thus, my new tablet in short, I can't stand. It's the same make and model except offers 4G which I don't use but it is unbearably slow (cant load my pdf vet school notes worth a damn- it's faster for me to find a computer, login to carbonite back up, download the enormous file and open it on the computer than to scroll through the pdf on the tablet one page per 10 seconds loading. It's truly unbearable. All the updates and changes are awful and its so slow despite me instantly ditching touchwhiz and using Nova Launcher.

Moment of silence for my beloved original, maybe one day science will advance enough for me to communicate with you without a working screen so that I can have you back. Laughingly, the one OS update I did do that slowed you down, turns out, compared to the ones that followed, you were still almost the speed of light comparatively.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White)

text_fidelity_a:
JOBY UltraFit Sling Strap for Women Horribly Uncomfortable.

What's the one thing that makes a good neck strap comfortable for long term wearing? Padding. What's the one thing this strap is completely lacking? Padding!

The part of the strap that's supposed to go around your neck is a two inch wide very rough textured bit of nylon webbing. Seat belts are softer than this material. The first time I tried the Joby UltraFit Sling Strap I carried my Kodak Z990 around for about an hour and it was so uncomfortable. Who designs a neck strap with NO padding?

This strap attaches to your camera via the ¼" tripod screw mount on the bottom of the camera. It's odd that your camera hangs upside down and I don't like the single point of failure mounting. Also, because of the way it's designed it puts angular force on the mounting threads when hanging and even more when releasing or engaging the quick release latch. Since the threads in my Kodak are plastic I have even more dislike for this mounting system. Additionally, you have to dismount your strap any time you want to use a tripod or monopod.

I found in the time I used this that the only time the (non) padded portion of the strap is on your neck is when the rig is retracted when you use the 'Speed Cinch' to bring the camera up for shooting, at least on my extra large frame, the whole strap rotates forward and puts the even more uncomfortable thinner strap around your neck and the 'padded' section down on your chest.

To sum it up... it's uncomfortable. It completely lacks any padding. It has an odd mounting system that puts lever like force on your tripod socket and you have to take the strap off to use a tripod or monopod. The only good point to this system is that it is rather well made. Unfortunately it's just well made junk. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone for any application.
text_fidelity_b: JOBY UltraFit Sling Strap for Women

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) We have a number of surface tablets in our house, and this was my first surface book. I got it hoping for some increased performance for using with my landscape CAD program, and I did notice a difference in the smoothness when working with CAD on this device as opposed to my other comparable surface tablets. The better performance only works when it is hooked up to the keyboard, which is fine for CAD work.

I also like to use this as a tablet for photo editing work related to my business, and here I noticed my number one complaint about this device, which is that the tablet part itself does not have the little foldout stand that all of the other surface tablets have. I guess they think that you will just connect it to the keyboard, but sometimes I want it to be as flexible and lightweight as a regular surface Pro tablet, and while you can unhook it from the keyboard and use it as a tablet, it feels more bulky and the lack of stand makes it less flexible in its use than the surface Pro tablets.

One thing I did notice is that you can connect it to the keyboard backwards and use the keyboard as a stand that way, however that does not bend to the same angle as the tablet stands do on a regular surface Pro.

I also think that the battery life is a lot less on this one than on the surface Pro tablets. Even when not connected to the keyboard and the increased computing performance that you get from that, it seems to wear down its batteries on tablet mode in about 30 to 45 minutes of photo editing. When I worked on my surface tablet in this fashion, I feel like I got a little less than two hours before having to recharge.

Overall, if you plan to use this primarily plugged in as a laptop and only occasionally as a tablet, the increased performance from the attached keyboard make this a worthwhile choice if you do gaming or more high-powered computing. However, if you are primarily using it as a tablet or in places where battery life is a critical consideration, I would suggest the regular surface Pro tablet instead.

In terms of accessories, I use the surface pen constantly, but haven't reached for the other accessories much at all. The surface pen makes it so smooth to make notes on photographs to convey ideas to people, and is great for photo editing.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB)

text_fidelity_a: Tile Mate (2016) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer The title is good at doing what it does, that being said, it's not a complete life changer. I believe it would be nicer if everyone in the world used a tile so that the software would be able to constantly locate a missing item but that's just not the case. However, we did lose a wallet in someone's car after being dropped off at home. The app last located the item at the house which was the last time the phone and wallet were together. After asking the person to look in there car, they were unable to find it. But one day when the phone was near that same car it was able to pick up the signal coming from the tile and we ended up finding it wedged deep down between the seats. That being said, if someone were to steal your item, it's probably not going to help but the way the tile works in telling you its last location is super useful.

But it’s not worth $170, especially when you factor in the incredibly expensive data that is the main selling point. i’m paying 50 bucks per month for 50 GB of prepaid data on T-Mobile. GlocalMe is $36 for 10gb and that’s US only. Usually when a company is trying to entice people to subscribe to expensive recurring service, they do so by providing a cheaper device. I haven't been able to stream anything from Amazon Prime, nor can I access the internet at all through the TV. So in complete frustration, without telling him, I ordered the Securifi Almond. Price was one factor in my decision, but I knew I wasn't going to be able to depend on him to help me set anything up and I'm not all that tech savvy.

One of the attractive selling points of this router is that it can be used either as a router or as a range extender. I planned to set it up as a range extender to see if I could get a better signal near my TV, but also had in mind that I might be able to persuade a certain somebody to try it as our router in place of the one that I feel like is defective (or just crummy) from our ISP.

I set it up myself. I just followed the installation on screen, and it was a snap. Fortunately, I knew what our log-in info was for our network so I didn't have to ask for help. I wasn't sure how it was supposed to work with the ethernet cable, so I plugged the Almond into the LAN port of of my TV and into one of the ports with a TV icon on the router. Then I tested it. Wow. The streaming is so much better than it was that I signed up for Netflix and started binging on "House of Cards." I still have the rotating download timer come up once or twice during an episode, but it gets done pretty quickly and the episode finishes playing. Before, I couldn't even load an episode or, worse, it would play a minute then completely drop the connection to the internet.

So I'm quite happy. This is a sleek little baby that works. I can see at a glance that I'm connected, which is reassuring. I haven't yet tried it in its router mode, but as a range extender it works great. You need to use the little stowaway stylus that comes with it when you're selecting onscreen functions, but as long as you remember to re-stow it, you've always got it handy if you need it.
text_fidelity_b: Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender

Sennheiser Momentum 3 Wireless - Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Alexa, Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App - White I ordered the 'New Sennheiser Momentum Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones with Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App' to review. So far, and after almost a month of testing and playing with these amazing headphones, I am ready to share my thoughts.

First and foremost I must express that I am really disappointed in the case that Sennheiser has included with these "High End" Headphones. I mean come on Sennheiser. It seems pretty standard these days for higher end headphones to come with a nice clam-shell hard case. The case provided is a soft zipper pouch with little to no padding at all. I would not feel comfortable to stuff these into my backpack or even suitcase for that matter.

Now with that said, these headphones ARE solid. The stainless steel headband is sturdy and not fragile. The headphones themselves are of a very nice quality construction with real leather, both on the headband and ear pads. The physical buttons (which I tend to like much better than the new "touch" buttons on some of the others out there) are nice and solid and function perfectly.

The sound is absolutely AMAZING! I compared them to my wife's Bose QuietComfort 35 II headphones and honestly I love the sound signature on the Momentum's better. And as for the Noise Cancellation, I honestly can't tell much difference between the two. I do think the Bose do a slightly better job but for the sound quality you get out of the Momentum's, I'll stick with the Momentum's.

As for the weight and comfort compared to the Bose, the Bose are lighter but not necessarily more comfortable. The Momentum's just feel SOLID. The Bose feel nice but light and flimsy.

Other thoughts - Others complain about the "auto pause" feature on the Momentum's, but I personally love it. Others complain about the way you have to power these off by folding them up and personally, it doesn't bother me a bit. I would rather that then pressing a button and wondering if you pressed it correctly. This way, you KNOW they are off.

Battery life isn't the greatest compared to many others in this price range but for me it's just fine. I don't travel long distances and for the occasional 5-6 hour flights I rarely take, they will give me what I need. Plus with the much appreciated USB type C charging port, they will charge pretty fast.

Overall I LOVE everything about these, except for the soft flimsy case provided. Sound is fantastic! They are loud with rich thumping Bass, Nice clean Mids and wonderfully crisp Highs and for me the Sound Isolation works great.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum 3 Wireless - Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Alexa, Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App - White

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150)) UPDATE: Six months in, this router has been flawless. AND I've discovered it has its own dynamic DNS support capability. That's a nice feature if you run any sort of server application. So, I continue to be impressed with this product.

---

I will be keeping a close eye on this router, which I just purchased yesterday, because it seems too good to be true. So far, in my 24 hours of usage since purchasing it for $29 at Walmart (sorry, Amazon, I was in a hurry) I have found it to be flexible and powerful in my unusual application, which is remote and requires 100% uptime with occasional bursts of heavy usage. Mine is a factory-fresh rather than refurb unit, incidentally.

I'll admit I had some trouble believing a router this cheap could be as good as this one turned out to be (assuming it stays reliable-- but, the one I bought trumpets a lifetime guarantee on the box). I expected something dumbed-down, with seriously constrained functionality and annoying firmware. (This model's v3 hardware, although Broadcom BCM5356-based, is not compatible with alternative firmware such as DD-WRT due to its problematic NVRAM size.) It's a single-stream design, with an internalized antenna, potentially suggesting performance limitations. And it's from Netgear, which I've frankly not had great luck with before... but it's been years since I've tried one of their products, and the reviews here are generally good. Most of the negative reviews here relate to support experiences, but my networking knowledge-level is expert, so ...what the heck, did I mention it was $29? An easy roll of the dice.

Though my application requires custom configuration, I initially started the unit using its web-based wizard, which you access by connecting your computer (via cable or WiFi) and pointing your browser to 192.168.1.1. With the unit connected to my cable modem, it set itself up quickly and voila, Internet. For most people this would be good enough and the job would be done. Kudos to Netgear for delivering the product with WPA-2 encryption enabled! They provide a SSID and password on a printed label. So, you're good to go. And its default configuration is just fine for most folks' usage.

For my application, however, I needed to cable several devices including a VoIP adaptor (a la [...] and a server with several ports exposed to the Internet. The unit needed to be set to a specific IP address scheme, SSID and password. And a dynamic-DNS utility on the server needed to communicate with my DNS provider. ...To accomplish these and other advanced tasks, the browser-based configurator at 192.168.1.1 has an Advanced tab. Proceeding through the settings is straightforward and similar to other reasonably-configurable routers. The default settings established earlier by the wizard remain intact in the Advanced panes so you are starting from a known-operable configuration. All good.

So I proceeded through each of my customizations, taking care to click the Apply button after modifying any pane. Usually there's a ten-second delay during which the unit sets up the new settings; a few necessitate that the router reboot itself. Everything went smoothly.

So, for $29 I'd replicated an unusual configuration and everything was working. But how well?

Okay so my wife had to take an important international FaceTime call as I was finishing up. So, for a while there the server was downloading some massive updates, two ssh clients were talking to the server, VoIP was in use, six WiFi clients were doing whatever they were doing, a 3G microcell tower was initializing and downloading firmware updates to itself ...and FaceTime was running smoothly with a high frame-rate on her third-gen iPad. A nice acid test!

In particular, I did not feel the need to mess with the unit's default QoS settings... and additional props to Netgear for including QoS in a router this inexpensive!

So far, I'm impressed. It's hard to imagine a better value in a router. I'll update this review if there are any reliability issues, but so far, so good. So excellent, in fact.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150))

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD

Pluged the UPS back in and the unit went back to the household current. PERFECT...

I highly recommend this unit. For the price, it cannot be beat!
UPDATE 8/22/14: Unit continues to perform well. I have installed the software, and find it very good. I don't know how long the battery will last before it will need to be replaced, but this was money well spent. I hope they produce this product for many more years.

UPDATE 7/9/16: The unit finally needed a battery replacement. So I got 5 and a half years life out of the battery. Not bad.....

text_fidelity_a:
Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers.

In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half.

What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases.

These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.
text_fidelity_b: Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet

text_fidelity_a:
Sony 4 GB Walkman Video MP3 Player (Pink) I had an iPod 2GB Nano and wanted to get something with larger capacity. I did some research and finally bought the Walkman. I was around for the very first Sony Walkman casette tape player, so the idea of getting a Sony MP3 player was appealing.
After using it for over a month, I find it a great little device. The battery life is amazing. I charged it over two weeks ago and have used it on multiple three hour car rides. I also had it hooked up to a speaker in my office and left it on for several hours and it stil has battery life.
It took me some time to get used to the navigation, but now I am fine with the difference between the Walkman and the iPod. The sound quality is good and although the volume could be better, it is acceptable for my use.
The major problem I have with the unit is the software. Sony included one of those mini disc's which loaded a couple of software programs on my computer. The main program is one which allows you to drag and drop files from your computer to the player; however, it doesn't work. I dragged a few tunes to see how it worked and then started dragging all the music. The software kept accepting the tunes, but after it "loaded" for about 2 hours, I discovered it had only loaded the first set of tunes. The rest, and the two hour wait, was for nothing. The software also has a "delete" function, which also doesn't work. It tells you that it delets items from the player, but they are still there.
So, I junked that software and decided to use the Windows Media Player. This is ok, except that the Media Player has a very odd way to create playlists. There are some round about ways to create the play list and I have finaly learned how to do it, but it took way too long compared to iTunes. The other odd thing is that when you create a play list it has to be from tunes on your computer, not on the device. Then when you sync the device to load the playlist, it may or may not put duplicate versions of the music on the device. Sometimes it finds the songs on the device and sometimes it does not. So, I ended up with multiple copies of some songs. The device software is also pathetic. It doesn't allow you to create playlists on the device, and as others have noted, there is no way to delete items from the device without using the software.
I finally just had the computer recognize the device as an external drive and was able to load songs and delete them with no probme.
Despite the isues, I still like the device better than my Nano. For one thing it has an FM receiver, which works great. Now that I have come to terms with the crappy software, it works great. So, if you are looking for an alternative to the iPod, this is a good option. Just stay away from the software provided by Sony and you will be fine.
text_fidelity_b: Sony 4 GB Walkman Video MP3 Player (Pink)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)) I drive in and around the Boston area, where none of the streets run north/south or east/west, every other intersection is a rotary, and a wrong turn down a one way street can take you an hour to correct.

The Nuvi is slightly better than trying to drive with a map on your steering wheel. I have been using mine for awhile now, and it mostly gets me where I want to go.

The problem is mostly how it does it. As many have already noted, there is no easy way to get it to show you alternate routes. And out of the city, especially, the route it gives you can be full of surprises. Take you off the highway and onto a dirt road for no reason whatsoever surprises. That happened to my husband on his way to a job in Hartford.

And forget trying to get around traffic. I was using it to get home from a doctor's office and saw that there was a ton of traffic on the route it was giving me through Harvard Square, so I turned toward another way home - one I do not know as well, but I know it is possible to get home that way - expecting the Nuvi to tell me it was recalculating and give me my next turn.

It did so, and I turned and followed the directions each time as it - get this - took me into the Harvard Business School parking lot and then out onto a one way street that put me on a no-turning-back 100% committed course to the traffic in Harvard Square.

Thanks, Nuvi.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer))

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer" My household has a variety of headphone fans in it. The headphone level of appreciation varies from "I will listen to anything as long as it works" to "I don't hear that sound exactly as I want to, so these are no good". I am in the middle. I love a good headphone, but I am not addicted to analyze every single sound and micro focus on them. What I am looking for is a headphone which has good sound separation, realistic presentation, but not too much distortion or muffled sound.

My purpose for wanting headphones with a cord was duo-fold. I want a set of headphones to listen to my desktop or laptop in my living room while people are watching TV, and I also wanted a set of headphones for my tablet so I could watch video demonstrations for my spinning wheel, knitting, and other crafts in the living room while the rest of the family is watching TV and I need to a quick refresher on a project I am working on.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
In the box (a nice box with excellent protection for the headphones), there is a set of headphones, two cords, and an extra plug adapter. The headphones themselves are lightweight for what they are. They are marked R and L so that you will put them on the correctly way easily. The ear cushions are a velveteen fabric which a lightweight foam inside. The cord jack is on the left ear phone. The top of the headphones has a soft leatherette foam which is very soft and easily squished.

The long cord measures about 118 inches. It comes with a large jack for stereos on one end and the smaller jack which fits into the headphones. The additional adapter for the smaller jack which fits into phones and tablets. The smaller cord measures approximately 48 inches and has a phone answering. This one has a smaller jack for phones and tablets.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES FIT?
I found that these headphones fit everyone in the family very nicely. Even my headphone fanatic liked them although he said his phones were a little nicer but not much.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I really like these. I have tried them with music, videos, movies, and other sounds from classes to classical. I find them to be realistic and high quality. It feels like I am in the room with the sounds - hearing squeaking of chairs, or fingers on strings - but yet it feels more natural than sound proof headphones. I can still hear what is going on around me, so if really loud music is happening in the room, these are not overly helpful, but that does not happen here so I am fine with them.

I found the sound clarity to be nice. No muffled sounds or blurry sound with these that I have noticed thus far. The bass is nice- not too much, but not overwhelming either. Of course, that depends on the recording I am listening to. There are no controls on the headphones.

Due to the cushioning these are comfortable. If I have a tender head (such as headache type day) they tend to hit a sensitive area of my head so I can not wear them as long as I would like, but most of the time, I can wear them comfortably for extended periods of time. It is nice because I can hear what is going on in the room around me if I need to so it does not block me from having to pay attention to things around me when necessary.

HOW DO THESE WORK WITH A TABLET?
I found these to work very well with my tablet. Using them for visual lessons at my spinning wheel and knitting chair is perfect- just what I wanted. I can hear what I need and not feel closed in with them on either.

CAN OTHER PEOPLE HEAR THEM IN A QUIET ROOM?
That is the one drawback about these headphones- if you are in a library, or quiet room, people around you will be able to hear what you are listening to unless it is very low volume and then you will have to strain to hear.

HOW DO THEY WORK WITH A PHONE?
I have not used them with my phone yet so have not had the chance to use the phone features. I tend to use my tablet most of the time. I will update when I have experience in that area to add.

OTHER COMMENTS
My son who is the headphone fanatic was even impressed with these headphones. He has several top line headphones (including Turtle Beach) and said that he was very impressed by the definition of sound, balanced bass and treble and clarity of these headphones. From him that is a compliment. He is rather stingy with glowing comments on most things electronic.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For the price of these headphones, this is a really nice set. Sound is clear, balanced, and realistic. The headphones are comfortable and well cushioned, making them wearable for extended periods of time. Lots of great sound and detail, yet the ability to hear the room around make them practical for use in a multitasking situation. They work great with tablets, laptops, and desktop although I have not tested a lot with my phone yet, my son has and they work great.

RATING
FIVE stars for these headphones. I am very happy with them. I plan to test in the future for gaming and phone answering and will update at that time.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer"

text_fidelity_a:
Laptop Stand, MISOTT Ergonomic Adjustable Laptop Stand, 2 in 1 Computer Stand Tablet Stand, Stand for Laptop Compatible with 10-15.6" Laptops and Tablets(Aluminum, Silver) This stand is perfect for my needs as I do not plan to carry it around. In 2018, I ordered a [[ASIN:B07HBQSCM3 Boyata Laptop Holder]] and love it. It has been working well for almost 2-years of daily use with my 14" LG Laptop. The Boyata will hold up to a 17" laptop. However, I wanted another stand to use for my "smaller footprint" tablets, so I decided on this one.

First of all, this collapses to a compact footprint as shown in the first few photos. Second, there is no assembly required. It is stylish (I love the flame cutouts) and simple. It arrives in a collapsed state and takes some strength to pull apart and move it into a desired angle.

I can adjust this to the angle that is most comfortable for me. I can also use this to angle my screen and also use a separate keyboard and mouse (which I can store underneath when not in use). This fits my 14" LG Notebook, my 12.9" iPad Pro, and my 10.1" Fire Tablet. It is not suitable for devices over 14". Although the Amazon page says it will work with 15.6" laptops, I do not recommend it as my 14" laptop hangs over each edge by 2.5" each side.

The anti-skid silicone pads on the bottom ensure that this does not slip around on my desk. The open flame design provides an opening for air circulation so the device does not overheat.

Only time will tell if the "hinges" on this stand will last and not collapse. I suppose if one changes the position of the stand daily, that this may not be so sturdy. Nevertheless, so far I love it for my purpose as I will be using this with my 12.9" iPad Pro or other smaller tablets I have. If it should fail in any way, I will update my review.

In summary, I do feel this is a nice non-portable stand option for laptops or notebooks under 14". I would not put anything above that size on this despite what the Amazon site says. The current price of $34.99 minus 30% brings the cost of this stand down to $24.50 which is exceptionally reasonable considering my other stand was $50.
text_fidelity_b: Laptop Stand, MISOTT Ergonomic Adjustable Laptop Stand, 2 in 1 Computer Stand Tablet Stand, Stand for Laptop Compatible with 10-15.6" Laptops and Tablets(Aluminum, Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Eversame Bundle of 3Pcs/lot Multi-color 6 FEET 2M Fabric Braided Nylon Ruggedized Micro USB2.0 Data Cable Durable Universal Charging Cord For Samsung Galaxy S4 S3 S2 Note 1 2 4 Tab HTC ONE M8 X NOKIA Lumia PDA X-BOX Motorola, LG Optimus G3, PS4 and Most Android Tablets/Android Phones/Windows Phones (Black White Pink) Most of the USB cables I have are either 3' cables or are really short ones that come with electronic devices. Sometimes a longer cable is really handy, especially when the immediate area surrounding a work space is cramped. I looked to these 10' cables to help alleviate one such issue and I learned a few things. One of those things is that a cable can be too long in some cases, though this is a failure in organization, not in the cable.

These are flat USB cables. Flat cables are less likely to tangle than their round counterparts, but I will confess to preferring round cables anyway (it’s a personal preference, not a technical preference). These are shielded in woven nylon which is great; the nylon is stronger than soft plastic shielding and gives the cable a little more stiffness but does not make the cable so stiff that it’s awkward to run. The connectors are interesting - two-tone plastic that is different than anything else on my desk which makes it a lot easier to determine where both ends of the cable are plugged in. I tried stressing the cable ends at the connectors by trying to pull out the shielding from the plugs and they held firm.

I tried one of these with my phone and it worked just fine, I was able to charge the phone and move data between it and my laptop. I did not attempt a speed test.

There is a big difference between 3' cables, 6' cables and 10' cables. If you need a 6' cable, a 10' cable will leave you trying to figure out what to do with the extra 4' of cable. If you need a 10' cable, these have worked great for me.

These are nice USB cables. They seem to be made well and they work as expected. If you need a really long cable, this is a good choice.

I have the RainbowLight color, which is exactly what it says: a rainbow light strip.

The rainbow light stays the same when turned on, the light doesn’t pulse or fade or change to any other color. The light can be turned on or off, there is no dimmer option. The rainbow light is visible when using your laptop.

The fan works well. It’s quiet and effective. The fan has a wheel to adjust the speed.

The cooling pad is height adjustable. The “legs” have two sections that fit into each other to adjust the height/angle of the cooling pad. It’s sturdy once you get the cooling pad set up, but I wouldn’t leave my laptop on it if I wasn’t there to catch it in case of something happening.

If using the cooling pad at an angle, the baffle is needed to keep your laptop from sliding off. The baffle is a small rectangle of plastic that stores in a designated spot under the cooling pad. There are no other safeguards built into the cooling pad to hold a laptop in place, so if you lose that piece of plastic, you’re screwed. I have other similar fans that have small ridges or foam pieces for extra security.

text_fidelity_a:
Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

So after some dumpster diving (or at least, I raided the battery recycling bins at work), I came home with batteries of various brands. For a while, I really did use recharged alkaline batteries exclusively and kept my Ni-MH batteries in the drawer. What I found was that I needed to change the batteries a lot more often and I couldn't be sure that the battery would have a charge when I took it out of the drawer.

Leaking is a big problem. My charger now has one charging port that is stuck because the liquid got in to the spring mechanism and dried. I also have a couple of remotes and devices that had to be cleaned out because the batteries leaked.

In the end, I had to give up on the idea of recharging cheap alkaline batteries because of how long it takes to recharge and that it can leak at any time, potentially ruining your device (mostly, it's just oily and you need to clean it out with a tissue). I just couldn't trust those batteries.

So why did I still give this charger 5 stars? Although alkaline charging was a failed experiment for me, the charger is still a better-than-average Ni-MH battery charger. It has separate intelligent charging and LCD display for each battery and will trickle charge a battery even after the lights turn green. Other chargers that have the same features cost more -- and without the Alkaline charging capability. You really can't go wrong with this charger.
text_fidelity_b: Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port

Lasmex HB-69 Bluetooth Headphone Over Ear, Hi-Fi Stereo Wireless Headset Ergonomic Protein Earpads丨Noise Reduction丨Built in Deep Bass丨Foldable Telescopic Arms丨Wired Mode for Travel Work TV PC Mobile I have worked with a lot of headphones, in particular active noise canceling (ANC) phones though I have several pairs of regular phones as well. One of the things that really bugs me about headphones these days is that there is a strong emphasis on bass, and most “bass enhanced” headphones overdrive the bass to the point that it destroys the rest of the sound profile in the process. This pair is one of the very few I have used that boosts the bass and gets it right.

Well, let’s get right to it – the sound profile is the most important feature of any headphones. If the sound is off, music will sound terrible and even straight speech can sound weird. These headphones tout their bass response, and I was a little apprehensive at first. However, unlike most, the bass on these is not so overdriven that it gives me a headache or interferes with the midrange. This is very unusual. The bass is definitely strong, but what is interesting is that it is actually detailed and not just a pounding low-frequency noise. I can hear details in the bass range that I usually can’t hear. A bass guitar sounds like a bass guitar, not a heavy noise frequency that is lost in distortion even at lower volumes. Even more interesting is that the bass, while stronger than the midrange, does not overpower it and drown it out, and the midrange sounds right. The highs are nice and clear too, without being bitingly sharp. Overall, the manufacturer did a very good job getting the sound profile right. It’s not exactly balanced because of the enhanced bass, but the enhancement is done well enough to make music still sound very natural.

Another area of surprise for me is that these are quite comfortable to wear for a little while even though they’re on-ear phones and not over-the-ear phones. I usually prefer over-the-ear phones that fit snugly, and these are the opposite of that. They’re on-ear and fit lightly, though tight enough to stay on when I tilt my head down and they do not pinch. These still have a little sound leakage when the volume is turned up a little, though it isn’t too bad at all.

These are Bluetooth phones and I was able to get them to connect to my phone very quickly and easily. Reconnection is quick and effortless.

Would I change anything? Yes – I would make these a tighter-fitting over-the-ear headphone. However, that’s a personal preference.

Overall, I am hard-pressed to find much about which to complain with these headphones. They get the bass enhancement right and sound really good. If you like headphones with a good bass response but still sound good, these are a good choice to consider.
text_fidelity_b: Lasmex HB-69 Bluetooth Headphone Over Ear, Hi-Fi Stereo Wireless Headset Ergonomic Protein Earpads丨Noise Reduction丨Built in Deep Bass丨Foldable Telescopic Arms丨Wired Mode for Travel Work TV PC Mobile

Screwdriver Set for MacBook, Tri-Wing Phillips Pentalobe 5 Pentalobe T5 Pentalobe T6 Screwdrivers Repair Tool Kit for Apple MacBook Mac Retina Pro Air This tool set is almost perfect! I’ll start with a little background... I am tech savvy for the most part, and I refurbish my own electronics, as well as stuff for friends and family from time to time. My MacBook Pro was bogged down by a “feature” known as thermal throttling. When older thermal paste dries up, it fails to conduct heat as well, so performance takes a nose dive in favor of preservation.

I’m not entirely sure if Apple actually does this servicing upon request, or not, but I honestly wouldn’t think that they do. So, after figuring out what was going on with my laptop, I rolled up my sleeves, brought out the few electronics tools I had around, and proceeded to gut my MacBook. Bad idea. You ever hear that saying about not bringing a knife to a gunfight? It went about that well.

Long story short, I busted a clip off of the motherboard that would have held the keyboard ribbon cable in place, and you can’t really just replace the clip on a motherboard, you have to replace the entire board. If I had this tool set in time for that repair, I could have saved the cost of replacing the board.

That said, these arrived in time for me to do the motherboard swap, and before I did (managed to upgrade to the i7 processor from the i5, a mild boost in performance I’m sure.) I made sure to once again, remove the heat sync, and remove the old thermal paste, replacing it with fresh TG-7. My geekbench scores now come in above what is average for the i7 version of my MacBook Pro. Above average is virtually unheard of. It’s like a brand new machine.

But these tools, if you attempt to do a repair without them, you could end up costing yourself a few hundred extra dollars. Learn from my mistake!

My only negatives here are for the durability and sturdiness, because I feel like the plastic spudger thing is definitely going to break eventually at the sharp pointy side. I don’t trust the plastic much. Other than that, the kit is well worth it, and every Mac enthusiast who plans to repair their own machine should really have it.
text_fidelity_b: Screwdriver Set for MacBook, Tri-Wing Phillips Pentalobe 5 Pentalobe T5 Pentalobe T6 Screwdrivers Repair Tool Kit for Apple MacBook Mac Retina Pro Air
